---
title: "Early versus standard Wnt"
---

## Biological insights from deconvolution algorithms applied to mouse gastruloids {#sec-bio-deconv}

@fig-bio-early contrasts a standard Wnt pulse at 48 h with a premature
pulse at 24 h, at three bulk-matched time points: 48 h, 72 h and 96 h.
@sec-bio-figure says what the figure can and cannot support;
@sec-bio-interpretation gives the biological reading.

### The figure and its statistical reading {#sec-bio-figure}

@fig-bio-early is a raster illustration, not a plot of estimates.
Panels A and B draw trajectories; the six bar thumbnails of panel C
carry no axis, scale or value. No deconvolution output exists in this
repository yet: the comparator runs of @sec-deconv-models are planned,
not run. What follows reads the figure qualitatively and lists what its
claims would need. Readings marked *(ours)* are not in the figure.

- **The consensus is on direction, not on point estimates.** Panel C
  reports that BayesPrism, SCDC and DWLS agree on the direction of
  change between arms (ectopic pluripotency up, primitive streak and
  pre-somitic mesoderm down in the early arm) and not on absolute
  abundances. Only that direction is carried into
  @sec-bio-interpretation.
- **Why absolute abundances disagree.** The figure attributes the
  disagreement to weighted least squares and marker weighting, which
  are sensitive to collinearity among closely related states. When
  neighbouring states have close mean profiles on the panel (candidates
  here, not yet checked: naïve, exiting naïve and epiblast at 48 h;
  pre-somitic mesoderm and somite differentiation front at 96 h), the
  signature is ill-conditioned, and a small change of gene weights
  moves mass between neighbours
  ([3.1, condition number](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-kappa-limits)).
  *(Ours.)* Collinearity affects every method that inverts the same
  signature, BayesPrism included; it separates methods only through
  their weights. Panel C groups SCDC, a weighted least squares, with
  BayesPrism, a multinomial likelihood, and sets DWLS apart, which
  points at the dampened weights of DWLS
  [@tsoucasAccurateEstimationCelltype2019] rather than at least squares
  as such. Testing this needs the condition number of the panel
  signature at each time and the per-method estimates.
- **Why direction can agree when levels do not.** *(Ours.)* At one time
  both arms are deconvolved with the same reference and panel. A method
  bias that multiplies the proportion of a type by a fixed factor
  cancels in the log-ratio contrast between arms; a bias that moves mass
  between collinear neighbours depends on the sample and does not
  cancel. Proportions are also closed: a rise of ectopic pluripotency
  forces other types down, so "ectopic pluripotency up" and "primitive
  streak down" are not two independent findings. The redraw therefore
  reads contrasts on centred log-ratios within each sample.
- **Uncertainty the claims need.** *(Ours.)*
  - A per-algorithm interval for every proportion: from the method's
    own uncertainty model where it has one (BayesPrism samples a
    posterior), and from resampling reference cells within type
    otherwise, which also carries the uncertainty of the one-specimen
    reference (@sec-geo-design).
  - A bootstrap over bulk replicates within arm and time, since the
    replicate is the unit of the arm effect, not the gene or the cell.
    There are three replicates per arm and time
    (@fig-suppinger-design), so a resample takes only 10 distinct
    values per arm; the redraw shows the nine pairwise early-minus-standard
    differences beside the percentile interval.
  - Panel C also states that control gastruloids vary more. A variance
    from three replicates has two degrees of freedom, and its 95 %
    chi-square interval spans a factor of about 150, so that claim
    needs more replicates or a model that pools across types and times.
- **How to read agreement across methods.** *(Ours.)* The methods share
  the reference, the panel and the bulk, so their errors are
  correlated, and agreement of three methods is not three independent
  confirmations. Two failure modes are shared by all of them. The
  early-Wnt bulk has no single-cell counterpart at any time
  (@sec-fs-bulk-consistency), so a state specific to that arm is forced
  onto the nearest reference types. And several states drawn in panels
  A and B (caudal epiblast, neuromesodermal progenitors) are not among
  the scored reference types of @tbl-fs-cell-counts, so no
  deconvolution against those references can return them. Sign
  agreement across methods is therefore necessary, not sufficient. A
  proposed reporting rule for the redraw: call a direction when every
  method gives the same sign and, for each method, the nine replicate
  pairs share that sign; report a per-sample goodness of fit on the
  early arm beside it.

### Biological interpretation {#sec-bio-interpretation}

On the **control-like** arm, 72 h is primitive-streak enriched and 96 h
shows pre-somitic mesoderm and somite progression. On the **early Wnt**
arm, 48 h retains more naïve pluripotency, 72 h is dominated by ectopic
pluripotency with a reduced primitive streak, and 96 h nearly loses
pre-somitic mesoderm. Absolute abundances disagree across algorithms
(@sec-bio-figure), so we treat the **direction of change** (ectopic
pluripotency up, primitive streak and pre-somitic mesoderm down) as the
consensus, not the point estimates.
